headline: 317/8: Bangladesh score 317 for 8 on Day 1 vs Afghanistan
summary: A strong opening partnership of 124 runs between Tanzid Tamim and Shadman Islam provided a steady start, but a middle-order collapse limited the progress.
details: Bangladesh finished the first day of the only Test match against Afghanistan at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi with a score of 317 for 8.
The day began with a dominant opening stand of 124 runs. Tanzid Tamim scored 83 off 41 balls, including a quick half-century, while Shadman Islam contributed 67 runs.
However, the momentum shifted as the middle order struggled. Mushfiqur Rahim was dismissed for a duck, and Muminul Haque scored 39 runs.
Najmul Hossain Shanto added 29 runs before being dismissed. Litton Das attempted a recovery with 53 runs, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz added 24 runs.
Despite the explosive start from the openers, the failure of the middle-order batsmen meant Bangladesh missed an opportunity to build a massive first-innings total.
caption:
A 124-run opening stand! Bangladesh starts strong but stumbles in the middle order.

Bangladesh finished the first day of the only Test match against Afghanistan at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi with a score of 317 for 8.

The day began with a dominant opening stand of 124 runs. Tanzid Tamim scored 83 off 41 balls, including a quick half-century, while Shadman Islam contributed 67 runs.

However, the momentum shifted as the middle order struggled. Mushfiqur Rahim was dismissed for a duck, and Muminul Haque scored 39 runs.

Najmul Hossain Shanto added 29 runs before being dismissed. Litton Das attempted a recovery with 53 runs, and Mehidy Hasan Miraz added 24 runs.

Despite the explosive start from the openers, the failure of the middle-order batsmen meant Bangladesh missed an opportunity to build a massive first-innings total.
